intro: Wet rooms have become one of the most sought-after bathroom upgrades in Sandal over the past few years, and it's easy to see why. Whether you're adapting a bathroom for accessibility, modernising an older property, or simply wanting that clean, open feel, a properly installed wet room adds real value and day-to-day practicality. The key word there is 'properly' — wet room installation is a job where cutting corners causes serious, expensive problems down the line. Getting it right in Sandal means working with someone who understands the specific challenges this area throws up, from the age of the housing stock to what's lurking behind those original walls.
localContext: Sandal is a mixed bag when it comes to property types, and that variety has a direct bearing on how wet room installation works in practice. The older stone-built properties and period cottages that sit throughout the area often have solid floors, irregular wall surfaces, and original plasterwork that reacts badly to moisture if the tanking isn't done correctly. These homes weren't built with wet rooms in mind, so extra preparation work is almost always needed. Modern estate homes in Sandal are more straightforward structurally, but they often have tighter floor-to-ceiling heights or en-suite spaces that require careful drain positioning. Sandal also sits in a moderately hard water area, which matters for wet rooms because limescale build-up on glass screens, tiled surfaces, and shower fittings is a genuine ongoing issue. Choosing the right sealants, grouts, and fittings that can handle hard water conditions, and advising homeowners on maintenance, is something a knowledgeable local installer will factor in from the start.
serviceDetail: A wet room installation in Sandal typically unfolds across several distinct stages, and understanding the process helps you know what to expect and why the timeline is what it is. The first stage is a thorough site survey — the installer checks the existing floor structure to confirm it can support a recessed drain without compromising joists or the concrete base, assesses the waterproofing challenges specific to your property type, and identifies where the waste run will exit. For stone-built and period properties in Sandal, this survey stage often turns up surprises like uneven floors or damp behind existing tiles that need addressing before anything else begins. Once the survey is complete, the floor is prepared and a linear or central drain is installed at the correct fall — usually around 1-2% gradient to ensure water drains efficiently without pooling. Tanking is then applied across all walls and the floor, typically using a specialist liquid membrane or tanking slurry system. This is the most critical stage of the entire job; poor tanking is the number one cause of wet room failures. After tanking has cured, tiling or chosen wall cladding goes in, followed by the shower valve, screen (if used), and any additional fixtures. A final inspection checks all seals, drainage rates, and water tightness before the room is handed over.
pricing: In Sandal, wet room installation typically costs between £6,500 and £12,000 for a full project, though the final figure depends on several factors. Older stone-built properties and period cottages usually sit toward the higher end due to the additional preparation work involved — levelling floors, extra tanking layers, and dealing with any pre-existing damp or structural quirks. Modern estate homes tend to come in at the lower end of that range. Room size, choice of tiles, the type of drain system, and whether you're adding underfloor heating all shift the price considerably. Fixture quality makes a big difference too — budget fittings in a hard water area like Sandal tend to degrade faster, so investing in quality here pays off over time.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Sandal well genuinely matters for wet room work. Someone familiar with the local housing stock — particularly the older stone-built homes and period cottages — will anticipate problems before they become costly surprises mid-project. They'll know the quirks of properties on certain streets, understand local building control expectations, and be reachable if something needs attention after the job is done. A local installer also has a reputation to protect within a relatively small community, which tends to concentrate the mind when it comes to doing things properly rather than just quickly.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built property in Sandal?
faqs.a: Yes, but it requires more preparation than a modern build. Stone-built and period properties in Sandal often have solid floors, uneven surfaces, and original plasterwork that needs careful assessment before tanking can begin. An experienced installer will carry out a proper survey first to identify any structural or damp issues and factor those into the project plan and quote.

faqs.q: How does hard water in Sandal affect a wet room long-term?
faqs.a: Sandal's moderately hard water means limescale will build up on screens, tiles, and fittings over time. Using quality grout and sealants suited to hard water conditions helps, as does choosing fixtures with easy-clean surfaces. Your installer should advise on a simple maintenance routine — regular squeegee use and occasional descaling keeps everything looking good and prevents build-up from damaging seals.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Sandal?
faqs.a: Most wet room installations in Sandal take between five and ten working days depending on room size and the condition of the existing space. Older properties with floors that need levelling or damp issues to resolve will take longer. Tanking also needs adequate curing time before tiling can start, so trying to rush that stage is a false economy.

faqs.q: Do I need building regulations approval for a wet room in Sandal?
faqs.a: You don't usually need planning permission for a wet room, but if the installation involves changes to soil stacks, drainage routes, or structural elements — more likely in older Sandal properties — then building regulations may apply. A reputable local installer will advise you on this during the survey stage and can liaise with building control on your behalf if needed.
